speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your gait and limb ataxia, could you please tell me how long these symptoms have been present and whether they started suddenly or gradually? Additionally, do you have any history of alcohol use or other significant medical conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of right-sided clumsiness alongside your gait issues is very important. To help narrow down the cause, do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Natalizumab use significantly raises the concern for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), so I need to check for other associated symptoms. Have you experienced any changes in your vision, speech difficulties, or memory problems recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of natalizumab use and these focal neurological deficits, I am highly suspicious of PML. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast. Do you have any cognitive changes or personality alterations?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain reveals lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI results confirm multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which is diagnostic for PML in the context of your natalizumab therapy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
